anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent image leaks the solution in two ways: (1) /conftest.py at the filesystem root contains a complete monkey-patched LogEI.__call__ fix with comments naming each bug, and because /testbed has no pytest inifile this conftest is actually loaded by the verifier's pytest run, so the LogEI test passes with zero source changes (verified: applying tests/test.patch to a pristine copy yields test_ei and test_logei PASSED, only test_pi FAILED); (2) the /testbed git packfile contains the unreferenced upstream fix commit 949a225 ('fix unittests', the direct child of HEAD) plus all later history, discoverable via `git fsck --lost-found` and `git log HEAD..<dangling>`, which shows the exact PI.py/LogEI.py diff and the updated tests. The remaining required change is a one-line PI fix that is readable from that commit, so the task can be solved by trivial file/repo inspection.

The agent image leaks the full solution: /testbed/.venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/aiohttp/ holds a non-editable installed copy of aiohttp whose web_fileresponse.py and web_request.py already contain the If-Range/If-Unmodified-Since/Content-Range/416 fix, so `diff -r aiohttp .venv/.../aiohttp` hands the agent the patch; the git pack also contains dangling future tag objects (v3.4.0a0 through v3.12.11) whose trees include the fixed file, recoverable via `git fsck --lost-found`. Additionally there is no tests/Dockerfile and tests/test.sh executes /testbed/mimo_test_command.sh, a file in the agent-writable repo that does not exist in the image, so an agent can plant a trivially passing script there and receive reward 1.0.

The agent image ships a pre-installed scipy 1.13.1 at /testbed/.build_env/.venv/.../scipy/sparse/linalg/_isolve/ whose _gcrotmk.py, lgmres.py, minres.py and tfqmr.py already contain the exact fix (@_deprecate_positional_args plus keyword-only `*` after x0), and the in-image /testbed/.build_env/test_command.sh explicitly points the agent at those paths. Running the patched test file against that pristine venv scipy passes all 32 new/changed tests, so the agent can solve the task by copying four files from the venv back into /testbed; the answer is embedded in the agent image and discoverable by trivial file inspection.

The agent image leaks the complete solution: /testbed/build/lib/mypy/plugins/dataclasses.py is a stale build artifact that already contains the upstream fix (arg_kinds check with the exact expected message '"field()" does not accept positional arguments'), while the source file mypy/plugins/dataclasses.py is unfixed. A trivial `diff -r mypy build/lib/mypy` or grep for 'positional' reveals both the patch and the exact error string the hidden tests require. The hidden tests themselves are correctly kept in tests/test.patch and the git history has no post-fix commits, but the baked-in oracle in the image layer is an obvious shortcut.

The agent image (/testbed) leaks the solution: build/lib/oauth2_provider/oauth2_validators.py is a stale build artifact containing the pre-#967 code with get_additional_claims(self, request) and claims.update(**self.get_additional_claims(request)), which is exactly the revert the task asks for, and the .git objects contain dangling future upstream commits (2022-2025) whose oauth2_validators.py also has the restored request-argument signature. The agent can recover the fix by diffing build/lib against the source tree or via git fsck, so the answer is accessible through trivial file inspection of the agent image.

The agent image leaks the full solution in two places: /testbed/node_modules/nopt is upstream nopt 7.2.1 whose lib/nopt-lib.js already implements the exact `typeDefault` feature requested (a diff against the repo's lib/nopt-lib.js is the answer), and the repo's .git pack contains dangling future commits (e.g. 6f22682 'release 10.0.0', reachable via `git fsck`) whose history includes commit 082bad3 'feat: allow setting typeDefault' and the hidden test file test/type-default.js verbatim. The verifier correctly keeps test.patch in its own image, but the answer is trivially obtainable from the agent-visible filesystem.

The agent image's /testbed repo has a local `master` ref 25 commits ahead of the detached HEAD, including upstream commit fc9438761 "Fix TableToTable issue (#195)", which is the verbatim grai-schemas fix the task requires (registering TableToTableMetadata in the edges Metadata union and correcting its attributes type); `git log --all` or `git diff HEAD master` exposes it, and checking out that file alone passes 3 of the 7 hidden tests. The leak is partial (the dbt adapter changes for endpoint-based edge typing, constraint_type enum values, and metadata merging are not in any ref), but the rubric explicitly requires that newer commits containing answers not be visible to the agent. Additionally, tests/ has no Dockerfile, so test.sh runs pytest from the agent-writable /testbed/.venv inside the agent container, leaving the test runner and the existing tests/conftest.py tamperable by root.

The reference solution is leaked inside the agent image: /testbed/build/lib/tuf/api/metadata.py is a stale build artifact that already contains the exact fix (Optional[bool] = None, pop('consistent_snapshot', None), conditional serialization), so a simple diff or copy against tuf/api/metadata.py yields the answer. Additionally, /testbed/.git contains 377 unreachable objects, including later upstream commits and a blob with the fixed metadata.py, recoverable via git fsck/cat-file. There is also no tests/Dockerfile, so the verifier runs in the agent's container and the agent (as root) could tamper with unittest or the tests package, though the leaked solution alone is disqualifying.

The agent image (xiaomimimo/mimo-v2.6-rl-oss:format-code-task-002755) leaks the full reference solution: /testbed/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/strawberry/ contains the post-fix versions of asgi/handlers/http_handler.py, fastapi/router.py, aiohttp/handlers/http_handler.py, django/views.py, file_uploads/utils.py, etc. (the exact try/except JSONDecodeError/KeyError handling, 'File(s) missing in form data' responses, and the FastAPI 404 change), while /testbed/strawberry/ holds the pre-fix source. A trivial 'diff -r strawberry .venv/.../strawberry' or copying the venv files recovers the answer; the stale /testbed/strawberry/**/__pycache__/*.pyc files also contain the fixed bytecode. Ground-truth tests themselves live correctly in tests/test.patch, but the solution is embedded in the agent image layers.

The agent image leaks the full reference solution: /testbed/build/lib/responses/__init__.py is a stale build artifact containing the complete upstream implementation of activate(assert_all_requests_are_fired=...) (get_wrapped with the mock.patch.object logic and the keyword-only activate signature), discoverable with a single grep of /testbed. Additionally the git pack in /testbed/.git contains unreachable upstream commits/blobs with the same solution code, retrievable via git fsck --unreachable and git cat-file. The verifier also runs in shared mode inside the agent container (tests/test.sh does cd /testbed and git apply), so no oracle isolation offsets these leaks.

The agent image (/testbed) contains the complete upstream solution in /testbed/build/lib/janitor/functions/complete.py and an identical copy in /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/janitor/functions/complete.py, both already implementing the requested fill_value/explicit parameters with docstring examples matching the issue. An agent can pass the hidden tests by simply copying that file over /testbed/janitor/functions/complete.py, so the answer is trivially accessible via file inspection in the agent image layers.

The agent image's /testbed/.git object store (766 MB) contains ~500 dangling commits descended from HEAD, including the exact upstream fix commit c602230de 'Correctly migrate resolvedImage type fields from legacy functions (#10060)' with its convert.js diff and the original migrate.test.js tests; a single `git fsck --lost-found` followed by `git log <sha> ^HEAD -- src/style-spec/function/convert.js` reveals the complete solution. In addition, the verifier runs the repo-owned `build/run-tap` script from the shared /testbed, which the agent can edit to force a passing exit code.

The agent image's /testbed git packfile contains the entire future upstream history, reachable via a dangling v3.21.1 commit (46c3d52) that `git fsck --lost-found` exposes; this includes the exact upstream fix commit c876329 'Ensure keys are non-keyword identifiers for TypedDict / NamedTuple', whose diff adds the isidentifier()/_KEYWORDS checks and the very test cases the hidden test.patch adds. An agent can trivially discover and cherry-pick the solution from image layers, so the answer is leaked in the agent environment.

The agent image's /testbed git object store contains 5179 post-HEAD upstream commits, including the actual fix commit 6d1706dbc ('SES: tolerate RegExp() without new, reenable tests', closes #230); they are not on any ref but are reachable from a dangling commit that `git fsck --lost-found` prints immediately, after which `git log <dangling> -- packages/ses/src/tame-global-reg-exp-object.js` or `git show 6d1706dbc` reveals the exact patch. The rubric explicitly requires that agents not see newer commits containing answers; additionally there is no tests/Dockerfile, so the verifier runs in the agent's container and executes the repo's own node_modules tap binary, which the agent could tamper with.

The agent image (/testbed, built from the mimo-v2.6-rl-oss base) ships a newer handlebars 4.7.9 under node_modules/handlebars (pulled in transitively by istanbul) whose lib/precompiler.js contains the complete upstream fix: the require.resolve('uglify-js') try/catch, the MODULE_NOT_FOUND check with rethrow, and the exact 'Code minimization is disabled due to missing uglify-js dependency' string that the hidden test asserts against. A trivial grep for 'uglify' or 'minimization' inside node_modules reveals the answer, so the solution is leaked through agent-image layers even though the hidden spec patch itself correctly lives only in the verifier (tests/test.patch) and the git repo contains no future commits with the fix.

The agent image's /testbed/.git contains dangling future commits (e.g. 1f5616cdd8 dated May 2026, 3053 commits ahead of HEAD) reachable via `git fsck --lost-found`, whose history includes the upstream fix commit db0af2151b 'Fix bitstamp asset movement fee in extra_data' and a test_bitstamp.py that already contains the exact verifier test `test_asset_movement_with_fee_works_correctly`. The solution and the hidden test are therefore recoverable by trivial git inspection inside the agent container; additionally the verifier runs in the agent's container with no tests/Dockerfile, so the agent-controlled `mock_bitstamp` fixture/conftest could be tampered with to suppress the warnings/errors the test asserts on.

The agent image's /testbed git object store contains ~111 dangling commits from 2025 whose history is fully reachable; `git log <dangling> -- airflow/models/taskinstance.py` surfaces the exact upstream fixes (ce8ea66918 'Fix secrets rendered in UI when task is not executed (#22754)' and 2dc806367c 'Mask sensitive values for not-yet-running TIs (#23807)') and `git show` yields the complete solution diff. The ground-truth patch is therefore recoverable from the agent image via trivial git inspection, violating the requirement that the agent not see newer commits containing answers; the tests themselves live only in the verifier patch and the working tree is otherwise unfixed, but that does not offset the leak.

The complete reference solution is baked into the agent image: /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/sktime/forecasting/structural.py and /testbed/build/lib/sktime/forecasting/structural.py both contain the finished _predict_interval implementation and the capability:pred_int=True tag (the exact code the hidden tests check against), and /testbed/.git holds hundreds of dangling commits from far-future sktime history whose structural.py also contains it. The agent can obtain the answer with a trivial grep/diff or `git show <dangling>:sktime/forecasting/structural.py`, and the verifier additionally runs in shared mode (no tests/Dockerfile) inside the agent-controlled container via `bash -lc` and PATH-resolved python/pytest.

The agent image leaks the complete solution: /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/gpflow/experimental/check_shapes/checker.py (and /testbed/build/lib/gpflow/...) is a newer upstream build containing the deferred _ShapeCheck multi-variable-rank implementation, with the 'At most one variable-rank' assertion removed; all 11 hidden tests from tests/test.patch pass as-is against that installed copy, so an agent can simply copy it over /testbed/gpflow. Additionally, a dangling future upstream commit (6206625b, 2022-10-17) reachable via git fsck in /testbed/.git already uses the target 'return: [a_shape..., b_shape...]' spec, and the tests run inside the agent's own container so site-packages/conftest tampering is also possible.

The agent image leaks the solution: /testbed/airflow/executors/__pycache__/{celery,local}_kubernetes_executor.cpython-310.pyc were compiled from the fixed sources (timestamped before the reverted .py files) and contain the complete send_callback implementation, docstring, and error message, discoverable with a plain `grep -r send_callback airflow/`. Additionally there is no tests/Dockerfile, so the verifier runs `python -m pytest` inside the agent-controlled /testbed with the agent's PATH and login profile, making the test runner trivially hijackable (e.g. a /testbed/pytest.py shim or a python() function in /etc/profile).

The agent image's /workspace/repo/.git contains the upstream remote-tracking branch origin/master, whose tree includes the complete reference implementation aws/s3.go (304 lines with NewS3Source, Via, S3Object, NewS3Sink, AwaitCompletion) plus aws/go.mod and aws/go.sum. The agent can obtain the full answer with a trivial `git show origin/master:aws/s3.go` or `git checkout origin/master -- aws/`, which is exactly the leaked-newer-commits scenario the criterion forbids; the test patch itself living only in tests/ does not offset this.

The agent image ships a stray Python 3.12 virtualenv at /testbed/.venv containing modern Zope 6.1, whose OFS/CopySupport.py already includes the complete upstream fix (the View-permission cleanup in _getCopy, commented 'It may contain private objects that the current user is not allowed to see') and whose OFS/tests/testCopySupport.py contains the exact hidden test test_copy_cant_copy_invisible_items. A trivial grep of /testbed for 'invisible' or 'private objects' reveals both the solution and the verifier's test, so the answer is embedded in the agent image layers even though the verifier's own patch and test runner are correctly delivered only via tests/.

The agent image leaks the reference solution: the untracked /testbed/build/lib/pre_commit/ directory contains the fully patched upstream code (rewrite_command in hook_impl.py, 'post-rewrite' in constants.py/main.py/run.py, PRE_COMMIT_REWRITE_COMMAND env var), discoverable with a single grep for 'post-rewrite'. In addition, /testbed/.git contains dangling upstream commits from Nov 2025 (e.g. 1b32c50b, 3d173871) that include the complete post-rewrite implementation, retrievable via 'git fsck --lost-found' and 'git show'. The verifier correctly re-applies its own test patch from /tests, but the answer is trivially accessible through file inspection of the agent image.

The agent image's /testbed/.git pack contains the complete upstream fix as an unreachable commit (bc50a01 'Fix to set `vfile.value` if a vfile@5 is given', a direct child of HEAD) plus the full future history; `git fsck --unreachable` or `git fsck --lost-found` recovers the exact index.js fix and the hidden test/vfile-5.js and test/index.js blobs (b246dcb2, 69cd9253) byte-for-byte. The pre-installed node_modules/vfile5 alias further hints at the hidden test setup. The solution is therefore trivially accessible through file inspection of the agent image.

The agent image (/testbed, baked into the base image layer) ships a stale compiled aws_lambda_powertools/utilities/batch/__pycache__/base.cpython-39.pyc built from the SOLVED base.py: disassembly shows __call__(self, records, handler, lambda_context), an inspect.signature-based _handler_accepts_lambda_context flag, and _process_record passing lambda_context to the handler, none of which exist in the checked-in base.py. The .pytest_cache/v/cache/nodeids file additionally names solution-era tests (test_batch_processor_handler_receives_lambda_context etc.), so an agent can recover the exact implementation and expected API by trivial file inspection of the agent image.

The agent image leaks the complete reference solution: /testbed/build/lib/airflow/utils/trigger_rule.py, /testbed/build/lib/airflow/ti_deps/deps/trigger_rule_dep.py and the non-editable copy in /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/airflow/ already contain the ONE_DONE enum member and the full one_done evaluation logic (plus the baseoperator docstring update), while the working tree at /testbed/airflow does not, so a trivial `grep -r one_done /testbed/build` or `diff -r build/lib/airflow airflow` yields the exact patch. The .pytest_cache nodeids file also leaks the hidden test names (test_one_done_tr_*). Additionally allow_internet=true lets the agent fetch the merged upstream Airflow PR, and the verifier's git-apply step offers no protection against this leaked answer.

The agent image (base image xiaomimimo/mimo-v2.6-rl-oss:format-code-task-000195) already contains the solved files in image layers: /root/.pyenv/versions/3.8.20/lib/python3.8/site-packages/paddle/fluid/layers/distributions.py is the fully patched reference version (all check_type/check_variable_and_dtype calls for Normal, Uniform, Categorical, MultivariateNormalDiag) and site-packages/paddle/fluid/layers/detection.py is the verifier's type-checked roi_perspective_transform/locality_aware_nms, so an agent can discover the answer with a trivial grep and copy it into /testbed. Additionally, the verifier's test_command.sh overwrites detection.py with its own hardcoded correct implementation and only copies distributions.py from the repo, so the detection-op tests pass regardless of the agent's work.
